title: Breathing mechanism & lung volumes
examples: How does the diaphragm help us breathe?
What does a spirometer measure about breathing?
What is the difference between tidal and residual volume?

explain.say: The diaphragm is a large sheet of muscle under your lungs. It moves to change your chest volume.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the lungs. Look at the trachea, the bronchus and the bronchioles. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
When you breathe in, the diaphragm moves down, making your chest bigger. This creates space for air.
When you breathe out, the diaphragm moves up, making your chest smaller. This pushes air out of your lungs.
A spirometer traces help us measure the amount of air we move. They show different breathing volumes.
Tidal volume is the air you breathe in or out normally. It is your resting breathing amount.
In real life, when you run fast, you breathe much deeper than normal. This increases your tidal volume.

faq.q: What is the main job of the diaphragm?
faq.a: The diaphragm is a muscle that moves to change the volume inside your chest cavity. When it moves down, it helps you inhale air.
asks: How does the diaphragm affect breathing?

faq.q: What are spirometry traces used for?
faq.a: Spirometry traces are graphs that show how much air you can move out or in over time. This helps doctors check lung function.
asks: How do you measure lung capacity?
What does a spirometer graph show?

faq.q: What is the difference between tidal and vital capacity?
faq.a: Tidal volume is your normal breath amount, while vital capacity is the maximum air you can breathe out. You can breathe more than the tidal volume.
asks: Is tidal volume the same as normal breathing?
What is the maximum breath volume?

faq.q: Why is the diaphragm important for breathing?
faq.a: It is the primary muscle of respiration. Its contraction and relaxation create the pressure changes needed for air exchange in the lungs.
asks: What happens if the diaphragm stops working?

faq.q: Can I predict my lung volumes from a spirometry trace?
faq.a: Yes, the shape of the trace allows scientists to calculate various lung volumes. These measurements are key indicators of lung health.
asks: What can be calculated from a spirometry graph?
Does the graph show all lung measurements?

facts: The diaphragm contracts and moves downward during inhalation.
Exhalation is usually a passive process, relying on the diaphragm relaxing.
Tidal volume is the volume of air exchanged during quiet breathing.
A spirometer measures the volume of air exhaled over time.

quiz.say: A person breathes normally at rest. The volume of air they move in or out is the:
quiz.why: Tidal volume specifically refers to the volume of air moved during quiet, resting breathing.

wrong.0: This is the air that always remains in the lungs even after a full exhalation.
wrong.1: This is the total air you can move in and out, which is a maximum, not the resting amount.
wrong.3: This is the extra air you can breathe in after a normal breath, not the normal amount itself.

quiz.say: If the diaphragm moves upward during breathing out, what is happening?
quiz.why: When the diaphragm moves up, it increases the pressure in the chest, forcing air out of the lungs.

wrong.0: This is a measurement tool, not a description of the diaphragm's movement.
wrong.2: Inhalation requires the diaphragm to contract and move downward to create space.
wrong.3: The diaphragm's position changes depending on whether air is moving out or in.

quiz.say: A spirometer trace shows a steady, consistent flow rate. This trace is best representing:
quiz.why: A steady, regular flow rate is characteristic of normal, resting breathing patterns.

wrong.0: Peak flow rate is a single measurement of the fastest air speed, not the overall trace shape.
wrong.2: Forced expiration involves a rapid, forceful push of air, creating a steep curve.
wrong.3: This test measures the extra air you can pull in beyond normal breathing.
